in.breaks: Fails when the yield is rising because the US is the problem — a fiscal scare pushes yields up and the dollar down at the same time, which is the tell that it is a credibility story rather than a rate story.
in.mechanism: Money chases yield across borders. A higher US yield relative to everywhere else pulls capital into dollars to earn it.

out.breaks: Vanishes whenever bitcoin is trading on something of its own — an ETF flow, a halving, a failure.
out.mechanism: Bitcoin is priced in dollars and bought largely with borrowed ones. A stronger dollar is both a lower quoted number and a tighter world.

node.label: Dollar index
node.up: The dollar is stronger — the world's margin call gets more expensive
node.what: The dollar against a basket of rich-world currencies. Most of the world's debt is written in dollars, so a rising dollar makes everyone else's debt heavier without anybody borrowing another cent. It is the single most reliable tightening signal there is.
